CVE-2026-16554 is an integer overflow in print_string_ptr() when size_t is 32 bits. DHI builds this package only for 64-bit linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, where size_t is 8 bytes and the escape_characters counter cannot wrap at the reported threshold.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-67217 by backporting the JSON Patch atomicity fix as dhi-cve-2026-67217-apply-patch-atomicity.patch. The patch validates the required replace value and the move source and destination parent before deleting or detaching any member, so a malformed operation returns an error without partially mutating the target document.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-67216 by backporting the object-comparison complexity fix as dhi-cve-2026-67216-compare-object-members.patch. The patched cJSON_Compare() first verifies equal member counts and then performs one recursive object walk, eliminating the second traversal that caused exponential CPU use for deeply nested equal documents.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-67215 by backporting the recursive-duplication depth fix as dhi-cve-2026-67215-circular-limit-duplicate-depth.patch. The patch caps cJSON_Duplicate recursion at CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT (1000), matching the parser nesting bound and preventing deeply nested JSON Patch copy/add operations from exhausting the thread stack.

The DHI cJSON package patches CVE-2026-29036 by backporting the JSON Pointer decoding fix as dhi-cve-2026-29036-decode-pointer-inplace.patch. The patched decode_pointer_inplace() correctly consumes RFC 6901 ~0 and ~1 escape sequences and preserves unescaped bytes, so JSON Patch paths resolve to the intended object keys.

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.

statements.action_statement: Use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset (DoS via crafted XML with improper entity resolution) affecting libxml2 2.9.11-2.11.0. The DHI package ships the Debian trixie 2.9.14 repack, which is in the affected range. Upstream fixed this only as a side effect of the entity-amplification rework in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (v2.11.0): a large parser.c rewrite plus ABI-changing additions to the public entities.h and parser.h structures. There is no isolated upstream patch, and neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships a backport to their 2.9.x branches. The fix cannot be applied to the 2.9.14 source without breaking API/ABI version compatibility for consumers, so no patch is carried. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6653

This is an out-of-memory denial-of-service issue in TIFFReadEncodedStrip(). Debian treats it as unimportant with negligible security impact when applications follow the documented memory-allocation guidance, including TIFFOpenOptionsSetMaxSingleMemAlloc(). This is a tiff2ps CLI crash with no practical security impact for the DHI package. Debian marks the issue as minor/no-dsa, and there is no upstream fix available to backport.

This is a tiff2pdf crash through ijg-libjpeg behavior rather than a libtiff library flaw, and the Debian security tracker treats it as unimportant. The DHI package does not expose this CLI crash as a security boundary.

The original report has not been confirmed by the reporter after repeated attempts, third parties reported being unable to reproduce it, and SUSE analysis indicates the report is likely a duplicate of CVE-2017-9935. The DHI package treats this as a non-issue unless a reproducible upstream report becomes available.

The related upstream fix, commit 25f9ffa56548c1846c4a1f19308b7f561f7b1ab0, was included upstream before libtiff 4.0.9 and is present in the 4.7.0 Debian source used by the DHI package. The remaining memory-based denial-of-service behavior is not planned for a complete upstream fix and is not treated as a security-impacting issue for this package.

CVE-2015-5237 is an integer overflow in MessageLite serialization when a message exceeds 2 GiB. Protobuf 3.21.12 (the upstream version in this Debian source package) uses ByteSizeLong() and rejects serialization when ByteSizeLong() exceeds INT_MAX before allocating buffers (see src/google/protobuf/message_lite.cc in protocolbuffers/protobuf v3.21.12). Debian security tracking still lists the CVE as unfixed, but the shipped 3.21.12 sources include the upstream mitigation from protobuf 3.4.0+.

NULL dereference in dri2GetGlxDrawableFromXDrawableId() inside libGLX_mesa.so only triggers when an X11 server sends an unexpected DRI2_BufferSwapComplete event to a GLX client. NVD and Debian mark this disputed with no reproducible scenario; Debian security tracker lists no fixed version and urgency unimportant. Exploitation requires a malicious or buggy X display server, not input reachable by remote attackers against headless pkg-mesa consumers using GBM/EGL/Vulkan.

Buffer over-read in glXQueryServerString() is only reachable from a GLX client parsing replies from an X11 display server. The CVE is disputed because no common use case requires uninterrupted operation against an attacker-controlled server; Debian lists it unfixed with unimportant urgency. pkg-mesa ships headless GPU libraries for container/server workloads and does not expose a remotely controllable X server attack surface.

Segmentation fault in glx_pbuffer.c __glXGetDrawableAttribute() requires a GLX client to query drawable attributes from a malicious X11 server response. Debian and NVD mark the report disputed; no fixed upstream or Debian version exists. Triggering the fault requires control of the X display server, which is outside adversary control in typical pkg-mesa headless deployments.

NULL dereference in check_xshm() for the GLX XShm extension is only exercised when a GLX client negotiates shared-memory transport with an X11 server. NVD notes the CVE is disputed with no demonstrated scenario; Debian tracker marks it unfixed and unimportant. An adversary cannot drive this path without supplying a malicious X server, which pkg-mesa server/container consumers do not rely on.
